modificationDescription: Verified upstream API (Button.js, button.d.ts): label/icon/iconPos/loading/loadingIcon/severity/size/text/raised/rounded/outlined/link/plain/badge/badgeClassName/tooltip/tooltipOptions/disabled/visible, extends native ButtonHTMLAttributes Omit<'disabled'|'ref'>, React.forwardRef with no useImperativeHandle (ref resolves to raw <button>), default aria-label = label + badge. Ultimate decision: preserved verbatim per spec §18's convergent-evidence justification (Angular's already-built UButton independently arrived at the same boolean-modifier prop set, not a variant enum) — no React-native redesign needed. pt/ptm/ptmo excluded per spec §7. Ripple excluded per spec §6 (not a Phase 3 component). tooltip/tooltipOptions props wired to a real `<UTooltip target={internalRef} content={tooltip} {...tooltipOptions}>` render, matching verified Button.js line 136's composition exactly, second confirmation (with Checkbox, Task 16) of the approved ref-target-primitive-plus-prop-sugar Tooltip API decision.

Verified upstream classes/css object shape, .p-*->.u-* renamed, instance.x passthrough-fallback pattern dropped since pt is excluded. Ported from the extracted reference file's real class-name logic, not invented. Two Boolean(...) coercions remain (severity, label) at sites where the boolean-modifier value is a string|undefined, not boolean|undefined -- those two are a real type mismatch unrelated to the ClassValue fix below and stay by design. The other four coercions this file originally carried were removed after packages/react-core/src/base/component-base.ts's ClassValue type was widened from Record<string, boolean> to Record<string, boolean | undefined> (a pure type-widening fix, no runtime change -- classNames() already treated undefined and false identically), which is the correct general-purpose fix for every future boolean-modifier style module (checkbox/dialog/menu, Tasks 16-18) rather than a per-component local workaround.

Ultimate-authored test, adapting scenario coverage from verified Button.spec.js (the one PrimeReact-authored test file in the proof set) plus additional Ultimate-specific assertions (ref forwarding, boolean-modifier classes).

Ultimate-authored root barrel re-exporting all @ultimate/react submodules, no upstream equivalent file. As of Task 18, re-exports all five proof-set component barrels: ./button, ./tooltip, ./checkbox, ./dialog, ./menu.

Verified upstream (Tooltip.js, 571 lines, full read; Tooltip.spec.js, all 13 tests read): target-based component, resolves target via ref/HTMLElement/selector, imperatively addEventListener's show/hide events on the resolved node, portal-renders a role='tooltip' panel only while visible. Ultimate decision: intentional accessibility improvement (spec §9) — adds aria-describedby on the target while visible (verified absent upstream), additive to any pre-existing value, removes only its own owned id on cleanup; multi-tooltip-same-target explicitly a non-goal. data-pr-* attribute config channel and mouse-tracking excluded per spec §9 (not React-idiomatic, no Ultimate internal convention needs it).
Verified upstream classes/css shape, .p-*->.u-* renamed.

Ultimate-authored test, adapting scenario coverage from verified Tooltip.spec.js (show/hide on hover, disabled-element non-display) plus new tests specific to the aria-describedby intentional deviation (spec §23's explicit regression-test requirement).
Ultimate-authored barrel re-export, no upstream equivalent.

Verified upstream (Checkbox.js full read both halves, checkbox.d.ts full read): checked: boolean is a required prop (no defaultChecked/uncontrolled mode exists upstream), trueValue/falseValue let checked represent non-boolean values, onChange receives a custom event shape not a raw DOM ChangeEvent, real hidden native <input type=checkbox> plus a separate decorative box rendering the check icon, inputRef targets the native input specifically. No indeterminate prop exists in verified source — confirmed absent, not an oversight. No PrimeReact-authored test file exists for Checkbox (verified absent) — this spec file is entirely Ultimate-authored. Second confirmation (with Button, Task 14) of the ref-target-primitive-plus-prop-sugar Tooltip API decision. Deviation from the brief's literal Step 5 code: `id` is now applied to the root <div> (matching verified upstream's `rootProps.id = props.id`) — the brief's literal code destructured `id` but only used it inside the onChange event's `target` object, never applying it to the DOM, silently dropping a documented prop. Fixed to match upstream and keep the `id` prop functional; no test coverage change needed since no spec asserted the old (broken) behavior.
Verified upstream classes/css shape, .p-*->.u-* renamed.

Ultimate-authored test — no upstream test file exists to adapt from. Includes an explicit assertion that the component does not manage its own internal checked state (fully-controlled contract regression coverage, spec §23).
Ultimate-authored barrel re-export, no upstream equivalent.

Verified upstream (Dialog.js, 717 lines, full read): controlled via visible/onHide, already-correct aria-labelledby/aria-describedby/aria-modal/role='dialog' wiring (preserved verbatim, not a gap), composes FocusTrap+CSSTransition(->useMotion here)+Portal directly in its own render body matching the no-shared-orchestration-service pattern already proven by Angular's UDialog (ADR-020). Focus-return-on-close preserved (both frameworks independently converged on this fix), restored via useMotion's onAfterLeave hook rather than a synchronous effect. Deviation from the plan's literal single-state `if (!visible) return null` sketch: implemented upstream's real two-state maskVisibleState/visibleState + onExited model (here: `containerVisible` gating mount/unmount, kept true through the leave phase) because the literal single-state version unmounts the DOM node synchronously on the same render that flips visible to false, before useMotion's effect can ever call .leave() against an attached element — that would make the required useMotion integration a no-op and break the verified upstream focus-return-on-close/onExited contract. This is a react-core-consuming fix scoped entirely to this component (no react-core primitive was changed); useMotion's own contract (enter/leave/cancel against a caller-supplied ref) was used exactly as designed. Explicit boundary (spec §15): draggable/resizable/maximizable behavior verified present upstream but NOT implemented here — no such props, handlers, or UI exist on this component in Phase 3, per an explicit, separately-tracked scope decision. document.primeDialogParams global-mutation scroll-blocking replaced by react-core's private useScrollLock registry (Task 9).
Verified upstream classes/css shape, .p-*->.u-* renamed, draggable/resizable/maximizable-specific class slots omitted since those features are not implemented (spec §15).

Ultimate-authored test — no PrimeReact-authored test file exists for Dialog (verified absent). Includes an explicit negative regression test asserting no draggable/resizable/maximizable props/UI exist (spec §23, §33's explicit requirement), and a focus-return-on-close test.
Ultimate-authored barrel re-export, no upstream equivalent.

Verified upstream (Menu.js, 518 lines, full read; MenuBase.js, 89 lines, full read; menu.d.ts full read): dual-mode (popup:false inline role='menu', popup:true Portal-rendered overlay via show/hide/toggle), model-driven, aria-activedescendant virtual focus (line 476, no .focus() call on any <li> — verified and preserved, intentional divergence from Angular's UMenu literal-DOM-focus approach per spec §10, ADR-006), full keyboard set (ArrowDown/Up/Home/End/Enter/NumpadEnter/Space/Escape/Tab), disabled-item filtering via 'li[data-pc-section="menuitem"][data-p-disabled="false"]' upstream (replaced here, see below). Verified negative finding, confirmed and preserved: Menu.js does NOT import Tooltip. closeOnEscape defaults to true, popupAlignment defaults to 'left' — both confirmed against MenuBase.js defaultProps and preserved. PrimeReact's data-pc-*/data-p-*-attribute passthrough-derived selectors NOT ported (pt excluded per spec §7) — replaced with an Ultimate-owned data-u-menuitem/data-u-disabled convention (spec §10). Real conflict investigated with evidence, same defect class as UDialog (Task 17): the plan's literal `if (!visible) return null` single-state sketch unmounts the DOM node synchronously on the same render that flips visible to false, before useMotion's effect can call .leave() against an attached element, defeating the leave animation entirely for popup mode. Verified against upstream Menu.js's real two-state model (visibleState gates the CSSTransition's `in` prop; the DOM stays mounted via CSSTransition's own unmountOnExit until onExited fires after the leave transition genuinely completes, and ZIndexUtils.clear/unbindOverlayListener run in onExit/onExited, not synchronously). Fixed here by reapplying Task 17's proven pattern: a `containerVisible` state (initialized to `visible`) gates mount/unmount and stays true through the leave phase; useMotion's onAfterLeave hook (already part of the existing MotionHooks/MotionOptions type, no react-core or uix-motion change needed) is what actually clears the z-index, unbinds the overlay listener, and flips containerVisible to false, once the leave phase completes. Inline mode (popup:false) never toggles visible after mount, matching upstream's visibleState initializing to !props.popup and never changing for inline menus, so this two-state machinery is popup-mode-relevant only. This is a fix scoped entirely to menu.tsx — no react-core or uix-motion file was changed; useMotion's public contract (enter/leave/cancel, onAfterLeave) was used exactly as designed, matching the identical finding already documented on the Dialog.js provenance entry above. Post-merge review fix (commit ca83432): the inline overlay-listener callback passed to useOverlayListener was a fresh arrow function on every render, compounding a shared react-core bug (see the react-core/src/overlay/use-overlay-listener.ts entry below) that leaked the outside-click document listener past unbind/unmount; stabilized via useCallback. hide() now guards against re-entrancy (multiple independent triggers — Escape, outside click, Tab, item click, Alt+ArrowUp — could otherwise double-fire it) and defers onHide to useMotion's onAfterLeave hook rather than firing it synchronously at leave-start, consistent with the two-state model's timing. popupAlignment's dead data-u-popup-alignment DOM attribute (no CSS/JS consumer, upstream's real prop instead drives DomHandler.absolutePosition's imperative JS measurement) was removed; the prop remains on UMenuProps for API-surface parity with upstream, but real viewport-aware positioning/placement logic is explicitly deferred as outside this task's brief and its test coverage — not implemented here.

Verified upstream classes/css shape, .p-*->.u-* renamed. inputStyle/ripple-conditional root classes and submenuHeader class slot omitted (spec §7 pt-independent styling, submenus out of Phase 3 scope).

Ultimate-authored test — no PrimeReact-authored test file exists for Menu (verified absent). Includes explicit regression coverage for the aria-activedescendant virtual-focus contract and the verified no-Tooltip-dependency finding. Real conflict investigated with evidence and fixed: the plan's literal test used `fireEvent.focus(list)` before asserting `document.activeElement === list` — in jsdom/RTL, fireEvent.focus dispatches only the synthetic React onFocus event and does not call the element's real .focus() method, so document.activeElement never actually changes; the assertion would fail regardless of the component's own focus-handling correctness. Fixed by calling the real `list.focus()` DOM method (wrapped in RTL's act(), since the resulting onFocus handler triggers a genuine React state update outside RTL's own event-dispatch wrapping), matching the identical `openButton.focus()` pattern already established in dialog.spec.tsx. Also fixed a real typecheck error (`tsc --noEmit`) in the popup-mode test: the plan's literal `React.createRef<{ toggle: (e: React.SyntheticEvent) => void }>()` is a narrower ref type than UMenu's actual `React.ForwardedRef<UMenuHandle>` (UMenuHandle also requires show/hide), which tsc correctly rejects as a type mismatch even though the untyped test runner did not catch it; fixed by typing the ref as the real exported `UMenuHandle` type. Post-merge review fix (commit ca83432): the popup-mode test's name ("dismisses on outside click") did not match its body — it never actually dispatched an outside click or asserted dismissal, which is why the useOverlayListener stale-listener-reference bug (see react-core.json) went undetected. Strengthened to genuinely click outside and assert both DOM removal and onHide being called; added a dedicated leak-regression test (open popup, dismiss via outside click, dispatch further unrelated clicks, assert onHide called exactly once) — RED-verified against the pre-fix code (onHide fired 3 times) before the react-core fix, GREEN after.
